The durian varies from olive-green to yellow to brown and can be pendulous,
round, or oblong.  The fruit ranges in length from 20 to 35 cm and can weigh up
to 10 pounds.  The semihard shell of the durian is covered with short, pointed
spines that make the fruit difficult to open.  The hard shell protects the fruit from
bruises and damage when the ripe fruit drops from the tree.  The fruit 
itself is a capsule that divides into 
five lobes, or segments, when ripe.  
Each segment contains one or 
more brown seeds that are 
covered with a thick, creamy, 
strong-smelling pulp, the edible 
part of the fruit.
